name: Brazil
summary: Brazil taxes residents on worldwide income. Since 2024 (Law 14,754/2023) income and gains from financial investments abroad are taxed annually at a flat 15%. From 2026 (Law 15,270/2025) dividends from Brazilian companies above BRL 50,000 a month per company bear 10% withholding, and a minimum tax of up to 10% applies to total income above BRL 600,000 (full 10% above BRL 1.2 million). Inheritance and gifts are taxed by the states (ITCMD, capped at 8%; Sao Paulo 4% flat in 2026). No wealth tax.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Resident individuals: 15% annual tax on foreign financial investment income and gains (Law 14,754/2023); 15%-22.5% on other capital gains; 15% on Brazilian exchange-traded equity gains; 10% WHT on large Brazilian dividends plus the IRPFM minimum tax from 2026; state ITCMD on inheritances and gifts.
regimes.eligibility: Holders of a permanent visa are resident from arrival; holders of a temporary visa without a local employment contract become resident after 183 days of presence within 12 months (PwC Residence).

capital_gains.summary: Gains on financial investments held abroad (including foreign listed shares and funds) are taxed annually at a flat 15% under Law 14,754/2023, separately from other income. Gains on shares sold on the Brazilian stock exchange are taxed at 15% (20% day trades). Other capital gains (unlisted shares, real estate in Brazil or abroad) are taxed progressively: 15% up to BRL 5 million, rising to 22.5% on the part above BRL 30 million.

capital_gains.rate_basis: PwC Other taxes: 15% flat on foreign financial investments (from 1 Jan 2024); progressive 15%-22.5% capital gains (top band above BRL 30 million) for other assets incl. assets abroad; 15% on Brazilian stock-exchange gains. Top band rates used for a large private business or real estate gain.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Day-trade gains taxed at 20%. Individuals are not generally recharacterised as traders; business activity is normally carried on through companies.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Small monthly sales of Brazilian shares (up to BRL 20,000) are exempt (not re-verified). Foreign currency gains on cash held abroad follow specific rules.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide; gains on foreign financial investments taxed on realisation once a year at 15% with no deductions.
open_questions: Law 14,754/2023 text not opened; rate taken from PwC and Deloitte.
Whether IRPFM (minimum tax) adds anything for income already taxed at 15% is not analysed; it is credited and should not increase these rates.

dividends.summary: From 1 January 2026 a Brazilian company withholds 10% on the whole monthly amount when it distributes more than BRL 50,000 in a month to the same resident individual. Dividends also count towards the new minimum individual income tax (IRPFM): 0%-10% on income between BRL 600,000 and BRL 1.2 million and 10% above, with credit for tax already paid. Foreign dividends are taxed at a flat 15% annually under Law 14,754/2023.

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 10% (WHT and IRPFM top rate) for large dividend flows. Foreign: 15% flat (Law 14,754/2023, PwC Income determination). Credit for foreign tax under treaties or reciprocity (US, UK and Germany recognised) - PwC Foreign tax relief.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 10% WHT on dividends to non-residents from 2026 (treaty rates cannot increase it); 15%/25% on interest and royalties.
dividends.treaty_network: About 40 treaties (incl. Argentina, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Chile, China, France, India, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, Mexico, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, UAE); UK, Colombia, Paraguay pending. No US treaty (reciprocity recognised for credits).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Profits of controlled foreign entities held by individuals are taxed annually at 15% on an accrual basis (Law 14,754/2023); trusts are look-through.
open_questions: Mechanics of the IRPFM reducer (combined corporate + personal cap of 34%) not studied in detail.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax (the constitutional large-fortunes tax has never been enacted).

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Brazil - Individual - Other taxes

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal IPTU on urban property (Sao Paulo basic 1% residential); ITBI up to 3% on real-estate purchases.

inheritance.summary: ITCMD is a state tax on inheritances and gifts, levied on the recipient's acquisition at up to 8% (Senate cap). EC 132/2023 makes progressive rates mandatory and LC 227/2026 (Jan 2026) set national rules, including taxation of assets abroad, but each state must legislate. Sao Paulo (scored here) still applies a single 4% rate in 2026; bills for 1%-4% or up to 8% are pending.

inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts taxed by ITCMD at the same state rate (Sao Paulo 4%).
inheritance.regional_differences: Rates vary by state (2%-8%; Deloitte: progressive 2% up to 8%). From 2026 movable property is taxed by the state of the deceased's or donor's domicile; real estate by its location (LC 227/2026).
inheritance.important_exceptions: STF (Dec 2024): no ITCMD on VGBL/PGBL pension plan payouts at death. A transitional pending change: Sao Paulo bills PL 7/2024 (up to 8%) and PL 409/2025 (1%-4%).
inheritance.foreign_assets: LC 227/2026 allows states to tax assets abroad once they legislate; status in Sao Paulo for 2026 uncertain.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Movables: state of domicile of deceased/donor; real estate: state where located.
open_questions: Whether Sao Paulo can already tax foreign-situs assets in 2026 (STF Tema 825 required a complementary law; LC 227/2026 now exists but state law and anteriority rules apply) is unclear; scope set to worldwide conservatively.
Sao Paulo small-estate exemptions not modelled; Rio de Janeiro and other states use progressive scales up to 8%.

residency.tax_residency_test: Permanent visa holders are resident from arrival; temporary visa without local employment after 183 days in a 12-month period; Brazilians leaving remain resident for 12 months unless an exit process is filed (PwC Residence).

routes.name: Investor visa (VITEM IX / permanent residence by investment)
routes.requirements: Residence for investment in real estate or productive activity under the Migration Law (Decree 9,199/2017); amounts not researched.

routes.name: Retiree visa (VITEM XIV)
routes.requirements: Requires a minimum foreign pension; not researched.

corporate.summary: IRPJ 15% + 10% surcharge above BRL 240,000 + CSLL 9% = 34% combined. 10% WHT on dividends from 2026.

us_citizen_notes: No US-Brazil income tax treaty; Brazil recognises reciprocity for crediting US tax. US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax.
open_questions: ITCMD on foreign assets in Sao Paulo for 2026 deaths/gifts unresolved.
Law texts (14,754/2023 and 15,270/2025) not opened directly.
